findings.old_behavior: No --releasever-major or --releasever-minor CLI options existed. Users could only override $releasever via --releasever.
findings.new_behavior: Two new CLI options --releasever-major and --releasever-minor allow overriding $releasever_major and $releasever_minor variables independently.
findings.compatibility_reason: New CLI options are additive and backward-compatible (default=None). However, they introduce new public CLI surface that could conflict with custom wrapper scripts or plugin argument names, and the releasever_major/minor config values can now be set independently of --releasever, changing the semantics of variable substitution in repo files.

evidence.snippet:
general_grp.add_argument("--releasever-major", default=None,
                                 help=_("override the value of $releasever_major"
                                        " in config and repo files"))
        general_grp.add_argument("--releasever-minor", default=None,
                                 help=_("override the value of $releasever_minor"
                                        " in config and repo files"))

findings.why_not_internal_only: CLI options are public surface. --releasever-major and --releasever-minor are exposed as top-level DNF command-line arguments parsed by argparse.
findings.uncertainty: The new options are additive with default=None, so existing scripts passing --releasever alone continue to work identically. No existing behavior is broken.
findings.recommended_review: Verify that no existing wrapper scripts or DNF aliases use --releasever-major or --releasever-minor as custom arguments.
findings.test_recommendation: Test that --releasever-major and --releasever-minor correctly override $releasever_major and $releasever_minor in repo variable substitution. Test interaction with --releasever (e.g., --releasever=40 --releasever-major=5 should set releasever=40, releasever_major=5, releasever_minor=detected). Test with --releasever=/ (detect from root).

findings.affected_surface: Cli._read_conf_file method signature and call site
findings.old_behavior: _read_conf_file(self, releasever=None) - called as self._read_conf_file(opts.releasever) passing 1 argument.
findings.new_behavior: _read_conf_file(self, releasever=None, releasever_major=None, releasever_minor=None) - called as self._read_conf_file(opts.releasever, opts.releasever_major, opts.releasever_minor) passing 3 arguments.
findings.compatibility_reason: The call site in Cli.configure() now passes 3 positional arguments. Any plugin or subclass that overrides _read_conf_file with the old signature (self, releasever=None) will receive a TypeError at runtime when configure() calls _read_conf_file with 3 arguments. Although _read_conf_file is _-prefixed (private by convention), DNF's plugin architecture allows plugins to interact with the Cli class.
findings.why_not_internal_only: While _read_conf_file is _-prefixed, DNF's plugin system exposes the Cli class. Any plugin subclassing Cli and overriding this method would break at runtime when configure() is called.
findings.uncertainty: Low likelihood: _read_conf_file is a private method. No known DNF plugins override this method. The new parameters are optional (default=None), so direct calls with only releasever still work. Only the call site passing 3 args causes breakage for overrides.
findings.recommended_review: Check if any known DNF plugins or custom deployments subclass Cli and override _read_conf_file. If none exist, the practical impact is zero.
findings.test_recommendation: Create a minimal test harness that subclasses Cli, overrides _read_conf_file with old signature, and verifies that configure() call does not raise TypeError. This validates the practical compatibility impact.

findings.affected_surface: Releasever variable resolution logic in Cli._read_conf_file
findings.old_behavior: conf.releasever, conf.releasever_major, conf.releasever_minor were only set when releasever is not None after detection. Conditional assignment via if-blocks.
findings.new_behavior: conf.releasever, conf.releasever_major, conf.releasever_minor are always assigned using or_else priority helper: CLI value > auto-detected > existing config value.
findings.compatibility_reason: The restructuring is functionally equivalent for all backward-compatible input combinations. Both code paths produce identical config values in all existing usage scenarios. The only net-new behavior is when --releasever-major or --releasever-minor are explicitly provided (covered by PCA-0001).
findings.why_not_internal_only: The restructuring affects public config state (conf.releasever, conf.releasever_major, conf.releasever_minor) that may be read by plugins, custom scripts, or repo variable substitution. However, the behavioral changes are functionally equivalent and do not produce different observable results in any backward-compatible usage scenario.
findings.uncertainty: Very low uncertainty about functional equivalence. The or_else() priority chain explicitly replicates the old conditional logic with identical precedence rules.
findings.recommended_review: Confirm that the or_else() helper produces identical results for all old input combinations. Scenario table: (1) no --releasever, no config: auto-detect fills all; (2) --releasever=X: releasever overrides, major/minor from existing; (3) --releasever-major=X: directly overrides; (4) conf.releasever set from config file: preserved.
findings.test_recommendation: Covered by PCA-0001 testing. No additional standalone testing needed for this restructuring.
